new.n: Wabasis caves, Tower farm road bank, NW shore of Wabasis Lake
new.pl: Road bank on the C. O. Tower farm, NE¼ sec 29 T9N R9W, Oakfield Twp (1894 Kent plat), between the old lake road and the NW shore
new.st: Second candidate spot for Chief Wabasis' kettle: 'Some caves in the bank of the road bordering the lake on the farm of C. O. Tower were for a long time supposed to be its hiding place' (Grand Rapids Press, 1916). The 1921 Lakeview piece says the lake shores had been dug in many places with no trace. Michigan state lidar shows a ~300 m cut bank between the old lake road and the NW shore on the Tower farm; no cave mouths are visible at lidar resolution. Not found.
new.t: Look-only: lake road and private shore lots. The other candidate, the creek above the lake from the Stocking family account, is the pin 'Chief John Wabasis' kettle of treaty money'. Access: road right-of-way / private: permission.
src: Grand Rapids Press, 11 Jul 1916, p. 13, 'Doubts Skeleton Is of Chief Wabasis'

set.t: Two family accounts give a tight search box: S side of the creek, 1/2-3/4 mi above Wabasis Lake, ~10 rods (165 ft) back. Find Stocking's rusted pick/shovel = near the spot. Check the creek course on the 1938 aerial and LiDAR. Access: county park / private: check. The Grand Haven Tribune (19 Apr 1900) says the Five Mile Hill digger Baty came from a treasure hunt at 'Wabassee Lake', Kent Co., in fall 1899, so the kettle was being dug for by 1899. A Jan 1922 'Judge' Lapham dialect piece about two locals striking the kettle while hunting skunk is humour, not a recovery. Second candidate (Grand Rapids Press, 11 Jul 1916): caves in the bank of the road bordering the lake on C. O. Tower's farm were long supposed to be the hiding place; the 1894 plat puts Tower at the NW of Wabasis Lake (NE part of sec 29 T9N R9W, where a road meets the NW shore). Michigan state lidar shows a ~300 m cut bank between the old lake road and the NW shore there; see the separate pin 'Wabasis caves, Tower farm road bank'. An older version (GR Herald, 2 Jul 1899) has the gold buried near his place of banishment or dropped in the creek.
